Gaza’s displaced families remain trapped in makeshift shelters three years on More than three years into Israel's war on Gaza, displaced Palestinian families continue to live in overcrowded makeshift tents, struggling with a lack of basic hygiene facilities, cooking supplies and adequate protection from the elements. In Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, a family of seven shares a cramped tent with little privacy, relying on scraps of wood and other materials to cook amid shortages of fuel and essential supplies. Displaced residents say mattresses have worn out, hygiene products are scarce and the tents offer little protection from winter cold, summer heat, mosquitoes or rodents. Despite the ceasefire, Palestinians say restrictions on the entry of humanitarian supplies and prefabricated housing units are preventing them from moving beyond temporary shelter.
